claims.text: Rapidly quenched nominally equiatomic FeCoNiTi has a dual-phase microstructure containing an fcc solid solution and a hexagonal C14 Laves phase.
Adding Ti to FeCoNi produces C14 Laves-phase precipitates within the fcc matrix.
The resulting microstructure contains fcc/C14 interfaces.
The Ti-rich C14 phase induces antiferromagnetic coupling across the interface with Fe, Co, and Ni sublattices in the fcc phase.
Interfacial antiferromagnetic coupling suppresses the orbital-moment contribution of the fcc phase.
Suppression of the fcc orbital-moment contribution reduces the alloy's saturation magnetization.
Magnetically and structurally heterogeneous secondary phases can be associated with lower saturation magnetization and higher coercivity.
The C14 phase pins magnetic domain walls at fcc/C14 interfaces.
The hexagonal crystal structure of the C14 phase increases magnetic anisotropy.
Domain-wall pinning and C14-induced magnetic anisotropy collectively enhance coercivity.
The dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy should exhibit coercivity of approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.
The dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy should have lower saturation magnetization than single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloys.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys have coercivity capped at 100 Oe.
The coercivity limit of single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys is caused by insufficient orbital moments and the absence of phase-boundary pinning.
The proposed coercivity-enhancement mechanism applies only to dual-phase fcc/C14 systems and should not occur in single-phase fcc or C14-dominant alloys.
The strength of antiferromagnetic coupling and the anisotropy contribution may vary with Ti concentration and C14 phase fraction.
Spin-polarized DFT should be used to calculate the spin-resolved density of states at the Fermi level for fcc FeCoNiTi in an explicit fcc/C14 interfacial model.
Magnetic measurements on a C14-dominant comparator alloy should be used to isolate phase-specific magnetic transitions.
Failure to observe either increased coercivity with C14 content or antiferromagnetic coupling would falsify the hypothesis.
